sources.title: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) | Valuation Ratios (Q)
sources.content:
The valuation ratios from December 2020 through June 2026 exhibit a cyclical trend characterized by a period of contraction followed by a significant expansion in market premiums. A general decline in valuation multiples is evident from late 2020 until September 2022, after which a consistent upward trajectory is observed across most metrics, peaking in late 2024 and early 2026.

Price to Earnings (P/E) Ratio
:   The P/E ratio began at 36.00 and experienced a gradual decline to a low of 24.82 by September 2022. Following this trough, the ratio entered a recovery phase, climbing to a peak of 36.87 in December 2024. While some volatility occurred in early 2025, the ratio remained elevated, concluding the period at 34.97 in June 2026. [...] Price-to-Earnings (P/E) Ratio Dynamics
:   The P/E ratio experienced three distinct phases. First, a period of contraction occurred between December 2020 and September 2022, with the ratio falling from 36.00 to a low of 24.82. Second, a phase of stabilization followed from December 2022 to March 2024, with the ratio fluctuating between 25.69 and 31.52. Third, a valuation expansion is noted from June 2024 onward, with the ratio peaking at 36.87 in December 2024 and remaining elevated above 30.00 through June 2026. [...] Price to Operating Profit (P/OP) Ratio
:   The P/OP ratio mirrored the trajectory of the P/E ratio, starting at 31.00 and descending to 20.74 in September 2022. A subsequent expansion brought the ratio back up to 28.21 by December 2024. The period ended with a ratio of 29.11, indicating that the market premium relative to operating performance remained higher than the 2022 lows but below the 2020 starting point.

Price to Sales (P/S) Ratio
:   The P/S ratio showed a moderate decline from 7.82 in December 2020 to 6.28 in September 2022. From that point, a sustained increase is observed, with the ratio reaching its highest level of 9.66 by June 2026. This suggests a growing market valuation relative to the revenue generated over the latter half of the analyzed period.

sources.content:
The valuation ratios from December 2020 through June 2026 exhibit a cyclical trend characterized by a period of contraction followed by a significant expansion in market premiums. A general decline in valuation multiples is evident from late 2020 until September 2022, after which a consistent upward trajectory is observed across most metrics, peaking in late 2024 and early 2026.

Price to Earnings (P/E) Ratio
:   The P/E ratio began at 36.00 and experienced a gradual decline to a low of 24.82 by September 2022. Following this trough, the ratio entered a recovery phase, climbing to a peak of 36.87 in December 2024. While some volatility occurred in early 2025, the ratio remained elevated, concluding the period at 34.97 in June 2026. [...] Price-to-Earnings (P/E) Ratio Dynamics
:   The P/E ratio experienced three distinct phases. First, a period of contraction occurred between December 2020 and September 2022, with the ratio falling from 36.00 to a low of 24.82. Second, a phase of stabilization followed from December 2022 to March 2024, with the ratio fluctuating between 25.69 and 31.52. Third, a valuation expansion is noted from June 2024 onward, with the ratio peaking at 36.87 in December 2024 and remaining elevated above 30.00 through June 2026. [...] Price to Operating Profit (P/OP) Ratio
:   The P/OP ratio mirrored the trajectory of the P/E ratio, starting at 31.00 and descending to 20.74 in September 2022. A subsequent expansion brought the ratio back up to 28.21 by December 2024. The period ended with a ratio of 29.11, indicating that the market premium relative to operating performance remained higher than the 2022 lows but below the 2020 starting point.

Price to Sales (P/S) Ratio
:   The P/S ratio showed a moderate decline from 7.82 in December 2020 to 6.28 in September 2022. From that point, a sustained increase is observed, with the ratio reaching its highest level of 9.66 by June 2026. This suggests a growing market valuation relative to the revenue generated over the latter half of the analyzed period.
